license_summary.furharvester_license: Required for residents and nonresidents age 16+ to hunt or trap furbearing animals (including raccoons). Not required for coyote or groundhog HUNTING (a hunting license suffices). Under 16: no furharvester license needed when accompanied by a licensed adult (one adult per youth). Landowners and minor children hunting on their own property: no furharvester license or habitat fee needed.
license_summary.habitat_fee: Residents and nonresidents age 16–64 must also have paid the habitat fee.
license_summary.otter_bobcat: Furharvester license + habitat fee (if normally required) + CITES tag arranged through a conservation officer or designated DNR employee within 7 days of harvest; lower jaw or skull turned over at tagging.

permit_requirements: Valid furharvester license and habitat fee (if normally required).
Report harvest and arrange a CITES tag from a conservation officer or designated DNR employee within 7 days of harvest.
Skin the otter and turn over the lower jaw or skull at the time the CITES tag is issued.
CITES tag must remain attached to the pelt until it is sold or otherwise rendered unavailable for sale.
species.notes: Accidental capture during a closed season/area or over the bag limit: not penalized if captured during a legal trapping season or legal depredation control, a conservation officer is contacted within 24 hours, and the animal is turned over as soon as practical (108.8).

bag_limits.limit_notes: No more than 3 bobcats TOTAL per furharvester per season (hunted or trapped). Within that: 1 per person per county in the 26-county limit-1 zone; up to 3 per person per county in the 31-county limit-3 zone. Bobcats trapped in excess of the limit or in a closed area must be turned over to the department (no penalty).

seasons.notes: Open in 57 of Iowa's 99 counties (see zone county lists); remaining 42 counties are closed to bobcat harvest. Season opens first Saturday in November (Nov 7, 2026). A regular hunting license is NOT adequate — furharvester license + habitat fee required.

permit_requirements: Valid furharvester license and habitat fee (if normally required); a regular hunting license is not adequate.
Report harvest and arrange a CITES tag from a conservation officer or designated DNR employee within 7 days of harvest.
Skin the bobcat and turn over the lower jaw or skull at the time the CITES tag is issued.
CITES tag must remain attached until the pelt is sold or otherwise rendered unavailable for sale; taxidermy mounts must keep the tag in possession as proof of legal harvest.
species.notes: Accidental capture during a closed season/area or over the bag limit: not penalized if captured during a legal trapping season or legal depredation control, a conservation officer is contacted within 24 hours, and the animal is turned over as soon as practical (108.8). Bobcats accidentally captured after the season has closed or in a closed area should be released alive if possible, otherwise turned over to the DNR without penalty.

verification.confirmation_notes: IAC 571 Ch.108 text is the 07-22-2026 publication (IAB 3/4/26, incorporates ARC 0117D effective 4/8/26) — current law for the 2026–27 season. Cross-checked against the DNR's 'Iowa Hunting, Trapping & Migratory Game Bird Regulations 2026–2027' booklet (PDF created 2026-08-25): all season dates match (Nov 7 opener, Feb 28 close, beaver through Apr 15 2027, otter/bobcat limits and county zones). First Saturday of November 2026 = 2026-11-07 verified by calendar.
known_gaps: Scientific names are standard taxonomy, NOT stated in Iowa DNR trapping regulations. All are marked scientific_name_verified=false; weasel is null because regulations do not distinguish weasel species.

Muskrat special late season (108.1(2)) applies only on specific approved/posted state game management areas, federal refuges, and county conservation board areas — the dataset cannot enumerate those areas; zone is modeled as 'special_areas' with a descriptive name.
Bobcat county lists transcribed from IAC 108.7(2)/(3) and the DNR booklet p.33 zone map; 57 open counties verified consistent across both sources (26 + 31).

Depredation take outside seasons (Iowa Code 481A.87, and coyote damage authorization in 108.5(2)) is noted but not modeled as a season — the app should offer an override (e.g. 'nuisance/depredation permit') rather than blocking the log.
Full regulation text (trap placement rules, snare specs, roadside limits, exposed-bait corridors, trap tagging) is NOT in this dataset — it covers seasons, zones, limits, and permits only.

trap_snare_rules.title: Trap & Snare Rules
trap_snare_rules.intro: The short version of Iowa's trap and snare rules. Reminder only — verify with the Iowa DNR before you trap.

sections.heading: Traps
items: Check every trap at least once every 24 hours.
Tag each trap with your name and address OR your DNR customer ID (new for 2026–27).
Foothold jaw spread: no more than 7 inches.
No exposed bait within 20 feet of the set.
Road right-of-way setbacks apply — see the DNR booklet.
Colony traps must be set entirely underwater.

sections.heading: Snares
items: Loop no larger than 8 inches (bigger loops only in certain underwater or private-land-near-water sets).
No powered snares except when set underwater.
